scope: Original fictional English claim-support challenge authored independently of candidate identities, outputs, and existing fixtures. Labels are author judgments for a frozen offline comparison, not external or expert validation. Facts not settled by the supplied passages remain not established.

passages.text: Meral declined to lend the atlas because its binding had become fragile. No pages were missing: she had just checked the complete sequence. She said the atlas could travel once the binding had been repaired.

cases.claim: Meral intended to repair the binding herself.

citations.quote: Meral declined to lend the atlas because its binding had become fragile. No pages were missing: she had just checked the complete sequence. She said the atlas could travel once the binding had been repaired.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: Repair is a condition for later travel, but no repairer is identified.

passages.text: The sorting machine lets a packet emerge at the archive end only if the packet bears a wax seal. Luro's packet had no wax seal when it went through the machine, and the machine added no seals. The log does not name its eventual destination.

cases.claim: Luro's packet emerged at the archive end.

citations.quote: The sorting machine lets a packet emerge at the archive end only if the packet bears a wax seal. Luro's packet had no wax seal when it went through the machine, and the machine added no seals. The log does not name its eventual destination.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: The machine requires a wax seal for that exit, and this packet lacked one.

passages.text: Veya found the compass needle in the drawer for spare hinges. It was neither broken nor missing from the workshop. She put that same needle back into the compass; she did not fit a replacement.

cases.claim: Veya repaired the compass by fitting a different needle.

citations.quote: Veya found the compass needle in the drawer for spare hinges. It was neither broken nor missing from the workshop. She put that same needle back into the compass; she did not fit a replacement.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: The passage expressly identifies the returned needle as the same one.

passages.text: The cabinet stayed locked from dusk until the following dawn. During the night, a visitor left an envelope outside it. At dawn, the archivist read the envelope's letter and only then unlocked the cabinet.

cases.claim: The visitor wrote the letter before dusk.

citations.quote: The cabinet stayed locked from dusk until the following dawn. During the night, a visitor left an envelope outside it. At dawn, the archivist read the envelope's letter and only then unlocked the cabinet.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: Delivery occurred at night, but the writing time is not given.

passages.text: In the valley, every shellcrawler has paired whiskers and lacks wings. Shellcrawlers can be male or female.
Nemi kept a shellcrawler in her glass box. Neither its keeper nor the account of its capture identifies its sex.

cases.claim: The creature in Nemi's glass box has wings.

citations.quote: In the valley, every shellcrawler has paired whiskers and lacks wings. Shellcrawlers can be male or female.
Nemi kept a shellcrawler in her glass box. Neither its keeper nor the account of its capture identifies its sex.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: The identified species is expressly wingless.

passages.text: Orbel had a single strip of sailcloth thirty-six meters long. She cut four pieces of seven meters each, wasting no cloth. She kept the entire uncut remainder in a chest.

cases.claim: Orbel put twelve meters of uncut sailcloth into the chest.

citations.quote: Orbel had a single strip of sailcloth thirty-six meters long. She cut four pieces of seven meters each, wasting no cloth. She kept the entire uncut remainder in a chest.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: Thirty-six minus four times seven is eight meters.

passages.text: Pell repeated the market rumor that the windmill had been sold, stressing that he was passing it on without vouching for it. Tovan replied that no sale had happened. The chronicler recorded the exchange without checking the mill's ownership.

cases.claim: Pell repeated the sale story without endorsing its truth.

citations.quote: Pell repeated the market rumor that the windmill had been sold, stressing that he was passing it on without vouching for it. Tovan replied that no sale had happened. The chronicler recorded the exchange without checking the mill's ownership.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: His explicit disclaimer separates repetition from endorsement.

passages.text: The port register lists the Copper Finch as the vessel locally known as Skiff Seven. The two names refer to one boat, not to sister vessels.
The unloading log says Skiff Seven arrived with seventeen tile crates. Four were taken ashore, and no other crates were added or removed before the boat left again.

cases.claim: The Copper Finch belonged to the tile maker.

citations.quote: The port register lists the Copper Finch as the vessel locally known as Skiff Seven. The two names refer to one boat, not to sister vessels.
The unloading log says Skiff Seven arrived with seventeen tile crates. Four were taken ashore, and no other crates were added or removed before the boat left again.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: Identity and cargo handling do not establish ownership.

passages.text: The charter ink dried at 10:00, and the courier departed at 10:20. The seal was applied after the ink dried but before the courier departed. The scribe took a brief break at 10:12; the record does not relate the seal to that break.

cases.claim: The charter had already dried when the seal was applied.

citations.quote: The charter ink dried at 10:00, and the courier departed at 10:20. The seal was applied after the ink dried but before the courier departed. The scribe took a brief break at 10:12; the record does not relate the seal to that break.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: Drying is explicitly earlier than sealing.

passages.text: In Mirrel's drawing, a name could enter the final bowl only if it had survived the first draw. The clerk showed Oset's name in the final bowl before the winner was selected. No result of the final selection appears in the record.

cases.claim: Oset's name failed to survive the first draw.

citations.quote: In Mirrel's drawing, a name could enter the final bowl only if it had survived the first draw. The clerk showed Oset's name in the final bowl before the winner was selected. No result of the final selection appears in the record.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: That would exclude the name from the final bowl, where it was observed.

passages.text: Pell repeated the market rumor that the windmill had been sold, stressing that he was passing it on without vouching for it. Tovan replied that no sale had happened. The chronicler recorded the exchange without checking the mill's ownership.

cases.claim: Pell vouched for the truth of the windmill sale story.

citations.quote: Pell repeated the market rumor that the windmill had been sold, stressing that he was passing it on without vouching for it. Tovan replied that no sale had happened. The chronicler recorded the exchange without checking the mill's ownership.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: He explicitly said he was not vouching for the rumor.

passages.text: Seln opposed stopping every sailing from Glassmere. The harbor adopted a narrower plan: it cancelled the two scheduled night sailings, while the daytime boats continued to sail. The notice said nothing about changes to daytime departure times.

cases.claim: Some scheduled sailings were cancelled, but sailing from Glassmere did not stop entirely.

citations.quote: Seln opposed stopping every sailing from Glassmere. The harbor adopted a narrower plan: it cancelled the two scheduled night sailings, while the daytime boats continued to sail. The notice said nothing about changes to daytime departure times.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: The night sailings were cancelled and daytime boats continued.

passages.text: The library occupies the lower floor of Sable Tower. The council hall is a separate building across the square. The moon atlas lay on a desk inside the library throughout the meeting.

cases.claim: The moon atlas was inside Sable Tower during the meeting.

citations.quote: The library occupies the lower floor of Sable Tower. The council hall is a separate building across the square. The moon atlas lay on a desk inside the library throughout the meeting.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: The atlas was in the library, which is inside the tower.

passages.text: The reservoir float operates without fail: whenever it rises above the red line, it closes the spillgate and switches on the blue lamp. At noon it rose above the red line. The keeper's notebook does not mention a warning bell.

cases.claim: A warning bell rang at noon.

citations.quote: The reservoir float operates without fail: whenever it rises above the red line, it closes the spillgate and switches on the blue lamp. At noon it rose above the red line. The keeper's notebook does not mention a warning bell.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: The mechanism's stated effects do not include a bell, and its absence from the notes does not settle whether it rang.

passages.text: Seven bells hung in the salt tower. The keeper established that not all seven were bronze. She also established that none of the seven contained any iron. She did not record how many bells were made of each material.

cases.claim: At least one salt-tower bell was not bronze.

citations.quote: Seven bells hung in the salt tower. The keeper established that not all seven were bronze. She also established that none of the seven contained any iron. She did not record how many bells were made of each material.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: Not all of a nonempty collection being bronze entails a non-bronze member.

passages.text: Orbel had a single strip of sailcloth thirty-six meters long. She cut four pieces of seven meters each, wasting no cloth. She kept the entire uncut remainder in a chest.

cases.claim: The remainder could provide one more seven-meter piece, but not two.

citations.quote: Orbel had a single strip of sailcloth thirty-six meters long. She cut four pieces of seven meters each, wasting no cloth. She kept the entire uncut remainder in a chest.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: The cuts used twenty-eight meters, leaving eight; eight is enough for seven but not fourteen.

passages.text: The fair calendar schedules the market opening for the seventeenth of Marn. The procession is scheduled for two days after that opening.
The rehearsal notice schedules the first procession rehearsal for the day immediately before the procession. Marn has thirty days, and these notices have not been revised.

cases.claim: The first procession rehearsal is scheduled for the eighteenth of Marn.

citations.quote: The fair calendar schedules the market opening for the seventeenth of Marn. The procession is scheduled for two days after that opening.
The rehearsal notice schedules the first procession rehearsal for the day immediately before the procession. Marn has thirty days, and these notices have not been revised.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: The procession is on the nineteenth, so the preceding day is the eighteenth.

passages.text: The first festival gong sounded before the supply cart arrived at Lark Fen. The cart arrived before the ribbon was cut. A visiting painter set up an easel that same morning, but the account does not place that event among the others.

cases.claim: The painter set up the easel before the cart arrived.

citations.quote: The first festival gong sounded before the supply cart arrived at Lark Fen. The cart arrived before the ribbon was cut. A visiting painter set up an easel that same morning, but the account does not place that event among the others.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: Being on the same morning supplies no order relative to the cart.

passages.text: The first festival gong sounded before the supply cart arrived at Lark Fen. The cart arrived before the ribbon was cut. A visiting painter set up an easel that same morning, but the account does not place that event among the others.

cases.claim: The first gong sounded earlier than the ribbon cutting.

citations.quote: The first festival gong sounded before the supply cart arrived at Lark Fen. The cart arrived before the ribbon was cut. A visiting painter set up an easel that same morning, but the account does not place that event among the others.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: The gong preceded the cart, which preceded the cutting.

passages.text: Fen's travel letter said, "I saw a pale plume over the quarry, but I could not tell smoke from dust." The editor titled it Fire at the Quarry. Fen protested that she had not claimed there was a fire. No later inspection is described.

cases.claim: A fire actually occurred at the quarry.

citations.quote: Fen's travel letter said, "I saw a pale plume over the quarry, but I could not tell smoke from dust." The editor titled it Fire at the Quarry. Fen protested that she had not claimed there was a fire. No later inspection is described.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: The headline and uncertain observation do not resolve the plume's cause.

passages.text: Meral declined to lend the atlas because its binding had become fragile. No pages were missing: she had just checked the complete sequence. She said the atlas could travel once the binding had been repaired.

cases.claim: Meral refused the loan because several atlas pages were missing.

citations.quote: Meral declined to lend the atlas because its binding had become fragile. No pages were missing: she had just checked the complete sequence. She said the atlas could travel once the binding had been repaired.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: The atlas had every page, and a different cause is explicitly given.

passages.text: The first festival gong sounded before the supply cart arrived at Lark Fen. The cart arrived before the ribbon was cut. A visiting painter set up an easel that same morning, but the account does not place that event among the others.

cases.claim: The ribbon was cut before the first festival gong sounded.

citations.quote: The first festival gong sounded before the supply cart arrived at Lark Fen. The cart arrived before the ribbon was cut. A visiting painter set up an easel that same morning, but the account does not place that event among the others.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: The given chain places the cutting after the first gong.

passages.text: Fourteen small statues stood in the kiln room. Six were stone and the rest were clay. Exactly two of the clay statues were glazed; every other clay statue was unglazed. The stone statues were not described further.

cases.claim: Eight of the statues were unglazed clay.

citations.quote: Fourteen small statues stood in the kiln room. Six were stone and the rest were clay. Exactly two of the clay statues were glazed; every other clay statue was unglazed. The stone statues were not described further.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: Eight were clay in total, but two of those were glazed.

passages.text: Dema wrote in her journal, "Rul believes the bronze bell was stolen. I think it was merely misplaced." The journal contains no account of finding the bell or checking either explanation.

cases.claim: Dema stated that she believed the bronze bell had been stolen.

citations.quote: Dema wrote in her journal, "Rul believes the bronze bell was stolen. I think it was merely misplaced." The journal contains no account of finding the bell or checking either explanation.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: She states a different belief for herself and attributes theft to Rul.

passages.text: On the workshop clock, rope weaving ran continuously from 14:00 to 16:00. Flute practice ran continuously from 15:00 to 17:00 that same day. Neither activity paused. The apprentices also ate a meal, whose time was not entered.

cases.claim: Flute practice began only after rope weaving had finished.

citations.quote: On the workshop clock, rope weaving ran continuously from 14:00 to 16:00. Flute practice ran continuously from 15:00 to 17:00 that same day. Neither activity paused. The apprentices also ate a meal, whose time was not entered.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: Practice began at 15:00, an hour before weaving finished.

passages.text: Every musician at the reed festival was a registered guest. Some registered guests stayed elsewhere for the entire festival and never slept at the inn. The lodging list does not identify which guests were musicians.

cases.claim: At least one of the festival musicians slept outside the inn.

citations.quote: Every musician at the reed festival was a registered guest. Some registered guests stayed elsewhere for the entire festival and never slept at the inn. The lodging list does not identify which guests were musicians.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: The outside sleepers could be musicians or other guests; the two subsets are not linked.

passages.text: At Brindle Quay, the bell ceremony was delayed, not cancelled. Its morning slot was released, and the revised notice said the ceremony would begin after sunset. The notice gave no reason for the change.

cases.claim: The ceremony remained on the schedule despite losing its morning slot.

citations.quote: At Brindle Quay, the bell ceremony was delayed, not cancelled. Its morning slot was released, and the revised notice said the ceremony would begin after sunset. The notice gave no reason for the change.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: A delay and a new evening start preserve the ceremony rather than remove it from the schedule.

passages.text: Veya found the compass needle in the drawer for spare hinges. It was neither broken nor missing from the workshop. She put that same needle back into the compass; she did not fit a replacement.

cases.claim: Veya restored the original needle to the compass rather than replacing it.

citations.quote: Veya found the compass needle in the drawer for spare hinges. It was neither broken nor missing from the workshop. She put that same needle back into the compass; she did not fit a replacement.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: She returned the same needle and explicitly did not use a replacement.

passages.text: Anet, an apprentice at the amber foundry, crossed the rope bridge during the inspection. No apprentice other than Anet crossed it during that inspection. Several masters were present, but their movements were not recorded.

cases.claim: Exactly one apprentice crossed the bridge during the inspection.

citations.quote: Anet, an apprentice at the amber foundry, crossed the rope bridge during the inspection. No apprentice other than Anet crossed it during that inspection. Several masters were present, but their movements were not recorded.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: Anet crossed, and all other apprentices are excluded.

passages.text: At Brindle Quay, the bell ceremony was delayed, not cancelled. Its morning slot was released, and the revised notice said the ceremony would begin after sunset. The notice gave no reason for the change.

cases.claim: The revised notice removed the ceremony from the schedule altogether.

citations.quote: At Brindle Quay, the bell ceremony was delayed, not cancelled. Its morning slot was released, and the revised notice said the ceremony would begin after sunset. The notice gave no reason for the change.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: The notice retained the ceremony with a start after sunset.

passages.text: Seven bells hung in the salt tower. The keeper established that not all seven were bronze. She also established that none of the seven contained any iron. She did not record how many bells were made of each material.

cases.claim: Exactly one of the seven bells was not bronze.

citations.quote: Seven bells hung in the salt tower. The keeper established that not all seven were bronze. She also established that none of the seven contained any iron. She did not record how many bells were made of each material.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: At least one is established, but the number of non-bronze bells is unspecified.

passages.text: On the workshop clock, rope weaving ran continuously from 14:00 to 16:00. Flute practice ran continuously from 15:00 to 17:00 that same day. Neither activity paused. The apprentices also ate a meal, whose time was not entered.

cases.claim: Rope weaving and flute practice overlapped for one hour.

citations.quote: On the workshop clock, rope weaving ran continuously from 14:00 to 16:00. Flute practice ran continuously from 15:00 to 17:00 that same day. Neither activity paused. The apprentices also ate a meal, whose time was not entered.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: Their shared interval runs from 15:00 to 16:00.

passages.text: Everyone who keeps a reef clock in Nacre Hollow speaks Low Reed. Some of the hollow's gardeners keep reef clocks. Nothing in the town register describes the other gardeners' languages.

cases.claim: At least one gardener in Nacre Hollow speaks Low Reed.

citations.quote: Everyone who keeps a reef clock in Nacre Hollow speaks Low Reed. Some of the hollow's gardeners keep reef clocks. Nothing in the town register describes the other gardeners' languages.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: Some gardeners are clockkeepers, and every clockkeeper speaks the language.

passages.text: For the frost watch, the tower roster names Teral as night keeper and Onwi as day keeper. No one exchanged roles that day.
The frost-watch log records that the night keeper lit the beacon after the day keeper had left. It says the day keeper did not light the beacon that day.

cases.claim: Teral lit the beacon after Onwi had left.

citations.quote: For the frost watch, the tower roster names Teral as night keeper and Onwi as day keeper. No one exchanged roles that day.
The frost-watch log records that the night keeper lit the beacon after the day keeper had left. It says the day keeper did not light the beacon that day.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: The roster resolves the two roles used in the event log.

passages.text: Veya found the compass needle in the drawer for spare hinges. It was neither broken nor missing from the workshop. She put that same needle back into the compass; she did not fit a replacement.

cases.claim: The misplaced needle had belonged to Veya before the workshop acquired it.

citations.quote: Veya found the compass needle in the drawer for spare hinges. It was neither broken nor missing from the workshop. She put that same needle back into the compass; she did not fit a replacement.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: The account gives its location and handling but no ownership history.

passages.text: Pell repeated the market rumor that the windmill had been sold, stressing that he was passing it on without vouching for it. Tovan replied that no sale had happened. The chronicler recorded the exchange without checking the mill's ownership.

cases.claim: The windmill sale had actually been completed.

citations.quote: Pell repeated the market rumor that the windmill had been sold, stressing that he was passing it on without vouching for it. Tovan replied that no sale had happened. The chronicler recorded the exchange without checking the mill's ownership.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: The rumor and its denial remain unverified; neither settles ownership.

passages.text: Anet, an apprentice at the amber foundry, crossed the rope bridge during the inspection. No apprentice other than Anet crossed it during that inspection. Several masters were present, but their movements were not recorded.

cases.claim: At least two apprentices crossed the bridge during the inspection.

citations.quote: Anet, an apprentice at the amber foundry, crossed the rope bridge during the inspection. No apprentice other than Anet crossed it during that inspection. Several masters were present, but their movements were not recorded.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: Only Anet among the apprentices crossed.

passages.text: The library occupies the lower floor of Sable Tower. The council hall is a separate building across the square. The moon atlas lay on a desk inside the library throughout the meeting.

cases.claim: The desk holding the atlas stood beside the library's south wall.

citations.quote: The library occupies the lower floor of Sable Tower. The council hall is a separate building across the square. The moon atlas lay on a desk inside the library throughout the meeting.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: The building and room are given, but the desk's position within the room is not.

passages.text: At sunrise, twenty-seven boundary markers stood on the moor. During the survey, nine of these markers were removed and four new markers were installed. There were no other additions or removals that day.

cases.claim: Eighteen of the original markers remained after the survey.

citations.quote: At sunrise, twenty-seven boundary markers stood on the moor. During the survey, nine of these markers were removed and four new markers were installed. There were no other additions or removals that day.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: Removing nine from the original twenty-seven leaves eighteen originals.

passages.text: At opening time, the green storage jar sat on the table beneath the window. Evin later moved it to the top shelf and left it there until the shop closed. The account does not say where the jar's detached lid was kept.

cases.claim: At closing time, the jar's lid was beside it on the top shelf.

citations.quote: At opening time, the green storage jar sat on the table beneath the window. Evin later moved it to the top shelf and left it there until the shop closed. The account does not say where the jar's detached lid was kept.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: The jar's movement does not locate its detached lid.

passages.text: Everyone who keeps a reef clock in Nacre Hollow speaks Low Reed. Some of the hollow's gardeners keep reef clocks. Nothing in the town register describes the other gardeners' languages.

cases.claim: Every gardener in Nacre Hollow speaks Low Reed.

citations.quote: Everyone who keeps a reef clock in Nacre Hollow speaks Low Reed. Some of the hollow's gardeners keep reef clocks. Nothing in the town register describes the other gardeners' languages.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: The rule covers clockkeepers, not necessarily all gardeners.

passages.text: Along one straight north-south road, the orchard gate lies north of the pond, and the pond lies north of the forge. Each occupies a different point on that road. The watchhouse is mentioned on the map without a marked position.

cases.claim: The watchhouse stands east of the road.

citations.quote: Along one straight north-south road, the orchard gate lies north of the pond, and the pond lies north of the forge. Each occupies a different point on that road. The watchhouse is mentioned on the map without a marked position.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: Its position is not marked or otherwise given.

passages.text: Dema wrote in her journal, "Rul believes the bronze bell was stolen. I think it was merely misplaced." The journal contains no account of finding the bell or checking either explanation.

cases.claim: Dema favored misplacement over the theft explanation she attributed to Rul.

citations.quote: Dema wrote in her journal, "Rul believes the bronze bell was stolen. I think it was merely misplaced." The journal contains no account of finding the bell or checking either explanation.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: Her own stated view is misplacement, contrasting with the theft belief she assigns to Rul.

passages.text: Everyone who keeps a reef clock in Nacre Hollow speaks Low Reed. Some of the hollow's gardeners keep reef clocks. Nothing in the town register describes the other gardeners' languages.

cases.claim: No gardener in Nacre Hollow speaks Low Reed.

citations.quote: Everyone who keeps a reef clock in Nacre Hollow speaks Low Reed. Some of the hollow's gardeners keep reef clocks. Nothing in the town register describes the other gardeners' languages.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: The gardeners who keep reef clocks provide counterexamples.

passages.text: The opening of the cloud fair was moved from Tuesday to Thursday. The rehearsal stayed on Wednesday, as originally announced. Lantern hanging was completed on Monday. No time of day was given for the revised opening.

cases.claim: Under the revised plan, the fair opens before the Wednesday rehearsal.

citations.quote: The opening of the cloud fair was moved from Tuesday to Thursday. The rehearsal stayed on Wednesday, as originally announced. Lantern hanging was completed on Monday. No time of day was given for the revised opening.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: The opening is on Thursday, after that rehearsal.

passages.text: The port register lists the Copper Finch as the vessel locally known as Skiff Seven. The two names refer to one boat, not to sister vessels.
The unloading log says Skiff Seven arrived with seventeen tile crates. Four were taken ashore, and no other crates were added or removed before the boat left again.

cases.claim: The Copper Finch left again with thirteen tile crates.

citations.quote: The port register lists the Copper Finch as the vessel locally known as Skiff Seven. The two names refer to one boat, not to sister vessels.
The unloading log says Skiff Seven arrived with seventeen tile crates. Four were taken ashore, and no other crates were added or removed before the boat left again.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: The register identifies the boat; its log leaves seventeen minus four crates.

passages.text: The cabinet stayed locked from dusk until the following dawn. During the night, a visitor left an envelope outside it. At dawn, the archivist read the envelope's letter and only then unlocked the cabinet.

cases.claim: Reading the letter preceded the dawn unlocking of the cabinet.

citations.quote: The cabinet stayed locked from dusk until the following dawn. During the night, a visitor left an envelope outside it. At dawn, the archivist read the envelope's letter and only then unlocked the cabinet.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: The archivist read first and unlocked only afterward.

passages.text: The dye shed held eighteen drums, five of them unsealed. A wagon removed three of those unsealed drums. Nothing else entered or left, and no lids were changed before the evening count.

cases.claim: The drums removed by the wagon all contained blue dye.

citations.quote: The dye shed held eighteen drums, five of them unsealed. A wagon removed three of those unsealed drums. Nothing else entered or left, and no lids were changed before the evening count.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: Their seal status is specified, but their contents are not.

passages.text: Pulling the west cord makes the observatory shutters close. The sand timer can trigger the same closing action. The shutters were open when Ves left and closed when she returned; she did not observe what triggered the change.

cases.claim: The shutters were no longer open when Ves returned.

citations.quote: Pulling the west cord makes the observatory shutters close. The sand timer can trigger the same closing action. The shutters were open when Ves left and closed when she returned; she did not observe what triggered the change.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: Their closed state on her return is explicitly described.

passages.text: Seln opposed stopping every sailing from Glassmere. The harbor adopted a narrower plan: it cancelled the two scheduled night sailings, while the daytime boats continued to sail. The notice said nothing about changes to daytime departure times.

cases.claim: The daytime boats all departed later than originally planned.

citations.quote: Seln opposed stopping every sailing from Glassmere. The harbor adopted a narrower plan: it cancelled the two scheduled night sailings, while the daytime boats continued to sail. The notice said nothing about changes to daytime departure times.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: Continued daytime service establishes neither delays nor punctuality.

passages.text: The charter ink dried at 10:00, and the courier departed at 10:20. The seal was applied after the ink dried but before the courier departed. The scribe took a brief break at 10:12; the record does not relate the seal to that break.

cases.claim: The seal was applied before the scribe's 10:12 break.

citations.quote: The charter ink dried at 10:00, and the courier departed at 10:20. The seal was applied after the ink dried but before the courier departed. The scribe took a brief break at 10:12; the record does not relate the seal to that break.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: Sealing could fall on either side of 10:12 within the specified interval.

passages.text: At sunrise, twenty-seven boundary markers stood on the moor. During the survey, nine of these markers were removed and four new markers were installed. There were no other additions or removals that day.

cases.claim: All four newly installed markers were painted red.

citations.quote: At sunrise, twenty-seven boundary markers stood on the moor. During the survey, nine of these markers were removed and four new markers were installed. There were no other additions or removals that day.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: The account specifies their number but not their appearance.

passages.text: The dawn carriage always crosses the causeway at sunrise unless its brake is engaged. On the morning of the silver fair, its brake was disengaged throughout sunrise. Its cargo manifest was not included in the station record.

cases.claim: The dawn carriage crossed the causeway at sunrise on the fair morning.

citations.quote: The dawn carriage always crosses the causeway at sunrise unless its brake is engaged. On the morning of the silver fair, its brake was disengaged throughout sunrise. Its cargo manifest was not included in the station record.

cases.label: supported
